deckTitle: MedKayfab: General Surgery — The Surgical Scrimmage

cards.power: The Pecalith Jam. Archie starts with a belly-button ache and ends with a sharp, right-sided stab.
cards.lore: Obstruction of the lumen leads to intraluminal pressure spikes, ischemia, and eventually a Blowout (Perforation).
cards.gradeReason: Belly-button-to-right-flank migration is one of surgery's most performable teaching moments.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro watercolor. Subject: Cartoon fuse-lit appendix castle under siege. Mood: Escalating dread.

cards.power: The Chemical Riot. Pete floods the peritoneal space with bile, stool, or blood, turning the ring into a toxic swamp.
cards.lore: Inflammation of the serous membrane causes a massive shift of fluid, leading to hypovolemic shock if not drained.
cards.gradeReason: Flooding the ring with toxic chemicals is immediate, vivid, and demands a physical response.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro comic chaos. Subject: Skunk-creature drowning surgical ring in toxic flood. Mood: Toxic catastrophe.

cards.power: The Traffic Jam. Otis stops the flow. Everything upstream swells; everything downstream is The Ghost Town.
cards.lore: Obstruction is most often caused by Adhesions (scar tissue). Otis leads to severe Vomitus and distension.
cards.gradeReason: Traffic-jam metaphor is strong; the upstream/downstream split needs context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro cartoon. Subject: Hippo-blocker stuffed in a bowel pipe, everything backed up. Mood: Stuck, swollen.

cards.power: The Strangler. Val twists the bowel around its own blood supply (Mesentery), cutting off oxygen instantly.
cards.lore: This is a vascular emergency. If Val isn't Untwisted, the segment turns gangrenous in hours.
cards.gradeReason: A strangling twist that kills in hours — visceral, immediate, and perfectly performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro watercolor. Subject: Snake coiling intestine in a death-spiral blood cutoff. Mood: Fatal urgency.

cards.power: The Gallbladder Squeeze. Cathy tries to push a stone through a tiny pipe after a fatty meal.
cards.lore: Cholecystitis occurs when a stone blocks the Cystic Duct, causing the Gallbladder Wall to swell and inflame.
cards.gradeReason: Stone-collecting magpie is charming; Murphy's Sign needs one step of context to perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro cartoon. Subject: Magpie hoarding gallstones in a tiny bile-duct pipe. Mood: Waddling, congested.

cards.power: The Bile Backup. The pipeline is blocked by a stone or Pancreas-monster.
cards.lore: Conjugated bilirubin can't reach the gut, so it leaks into the blood and out through the skin and eyes.
cards.gradeReason: Turning yellow is the most visible clinical performance in the deck — instant recognition at any table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro watercolor. Subject: Ghost glowing sickly yellow, bile leaking from skin and eyes. Mood: Eerie, toxic.

cards.power: The Auto-Digest. Phil gets angry and releases his enzymes inside himself, cooking his own tissue.
cards.lore: Often triggered by Gallstones or Alcohol. Phil can trigger a deadly Cytokine Tsunami (SIRS).
cards.gradeReason: Self-eating is viscerally clear; SIRS cascade context needed to close the performance loop.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro comic. Subject: Goat-chef frantically digesting himself in a boiling pot. Mood: Frantic self-destruction.

cards.power: The Septic Storm. Chuck is the ultimate biliary emergency. Infection is trapped under pressure in the bile ducts.
cards.lore: Put under pressure (Charcot's Triad +). He needs urgent decompression (ERCP).
cards.gradeReason: Reynolds Pentad name is memorable but the five-criteria stack needs clinical context to embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro watercolor. Subject: Octopus-villain pressurizing bile ducts into explosive septic storm. Mood: Explosive, pressurized.

cards.power: The Escape Artist. Izzy finds a weak spot in the abdominal wall and shoves the bowel through it.
cards.lore: Indirect Izzy follows the Spermatic Cord; Direct Izzy just punches straight through the Hesselbach Floor.
cards.gradeReason: Escape-artist metaphor is excellent; Hesselbach anatomy splits the card into context-needing territory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro cartoon. Subject: Snake slithering through chain-link fence abdominal wall. Mood: Sneaky, relentless.

cards.power: The Death Grip. The hole is too tight to let blood can't get in, and the trapped bowel starts to die.
cards.lore: A Reducible hernia is a nuisance; a Strangulated Stan is a surgical race against the clock.
cards.gradeReason: Death grip / trapped bowel dying — racing the clock is immediately performable clinical urgency.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro dramatic. Subject: Crab claw strangling purple bowel through a tight ring. Mood: Desperate, dying.

cards.power: The High-Risk Escape. Fiona uses a tiny, tight canal. She is highly prone to rapid Strangulation.
cards.lore: The Femoral Canal is rigid and narrow. Fiona doesn't play the mechanical marvel—Fiona traps the bowel almost immediately.
cards.gradeReason: High-risk-escape role is clear; the anatomical distinction from Inguinal-Izzy needs a map to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro cartoon. Subject: Small mouse squeezing through impossibly narrow femoral canal, bowel in danger. Mood: Tight, precarious.

cards.power: The Scar-Breaker. Ina passes through the shock of a previous cut, where the Fascia-Armor never rebuilt.
cards.lore: Failure of primary healing. Ina is the reason surgeons choose over Future Tension.
cards.gradeReason: Mechanistic description of scarring rather than a role you can step into at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro worn. Subject: Armadillo bursting through a half-healed surgical scar in decayed fascia. Mood: Worn, inevitable.

cards.power: The Silent Bomb. Arthur waits. He grows slowly and painlessly until he suddenly Pops.
cards.lore: Weakening of the tunica media. If Arthur ruptures, the Scrimmage is done without instant OR access.
cards.gradeReason: A silent bomb that suddenly pops — perfect dramatic tension, zero context needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro suspense. Subject: Toad inflating silently inside a pulsing aortic wall, seconds from explosion. Mood: Ticking dread.

cards.power: The Gut Stroke. Mitch cuts off blood to the intestines. The patient screams, but the belly feels soft.
cards.lore: Embolism in the SMA. Without blood, the bowel lining dies, leading to massive bacterial invasion.
cards.gradeReason: Pain-out-of-proportion is a teaching point, not a character performance — reads as a clinical criterion.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro dark. Subject: Vulture severing mesenteric blood supply, bowel turning grey below. Mood: Ominous, silent.

cards.power: The Backflow. Vince occurs when the valves in the legs fail, allowing venous blood to pool in the ankles.
cards.lore: Chronic venous hypertension leads to severe skin changes and Ulcer Formation (Lipodermatosclerosis).
cards.gradeReason: Describes a mechanical failure rather than inviting the player to embody a character.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro lazy. Subject: Sloth draping swollen purple veins across a swollen leg, pooling downward. Mood: Sluggish, bloated.

cards.power: The Walking Stop. Claude starves the muscles of oxygen, making the calves burn after just 500 meters.
cards.lore: Atherosclerosis of the Iliac/Femoral arteries. Claude is a blaring warning siren of Global Vascular War.
cards.gradeReason: Calves burning at 500m is a concrete performance cue; ABI <0.9 stat keeps it slightly diagnostic.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro sturdy. Subject: Rhino blocking artery road, legs limping under ischemic load. Mood: Stubborn, painful.

cards.power: The Acid Burn. Percy eats through the stomach lining. The Acid Militia fires at the Gastroduodenal Artery.
cards.lore: Imbalance between gastric acid and mucosal protection. Perforation leads to lethal Free Air under the diaphragm.
cards.gradeReason: Acid militia eating the wall is vivid; H. pylori stat adds diagnostic context that softens the embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro caustic. Subject: Alligator burning through stomach lining with acid spray. Mood: Corrosive, relentless.

cards.power: The Retch-Rip. Mel occurs when violent vomiting tears the delicate junction between esophagus and stomach.
cards.lore: A longitudinal mucosal tear. Mel usually stops bleeding on his own, but the hematemesis is terrifying.
cards.gradeReason: Violent retching-to-tear is physically immediate; the self-limiting nature needs clinical context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro dramatic. Subject: Raccoon tearing the gastroesophageal junction with a retch scream. Mood: Violent, sudden.

cards.power: The Full-Thickness Blowout. Bob is the Final Level of Mel. The esophagus actually pops entirely open.
cards.lore: Transmural rupture leads to Mediastinitis, affecting the heart and lungs. A 911 absolute emergency.
cards.gradeReason: Full esophageal explosion affecting the heart and lungs — the most dramatic single card in the GI section.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro explosive. Subject: Pufferfish-villain blowing apart the esophagus entirely in a catastrophic blowout. Mood: Catastrophic, 911.

cards.power: The Food Trap. Ace keeps the Bottom Door of the esophagus locked shut. Food sits, stacks up, and rots.
cards.lore: Loss of the Myenteric Plexus. Ace needs a surgical Heller Myotomy to forcefully kick the door down.
cards.gradeReason: Food-trap metaphor is clear and embodied; Myenteric Plexus mechanism is educational rather than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro locked-door. Subject: Beaver bolting esophageal door shut, food piling behind a blocked dam. Mood: Obstinate, stacking.

cards.power: The Left-Sided Appendicitis. Dan occurs when tiny structural pouches in the colon get clogged and infected.
cards.lore: Diverticulosis is simply having the pouches; Diverticulitis is when Dan starts the inflammatory riot.
cards.gradeReason: Left-sided appendicitis framing is an excellent teaching hook; the -osis vs -itis distinction needs context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro messy. Subject: Hedgehog with infected pouches erupting along colon wall, left-sided riot. Mood: Cluttered, inflamed.

cards.power: The Silent Grower. Pete isn't cancer yet, but he's Applying for the Job.
cards.lore: Villous adenomas carry the highest risk. Snipping Pete out during a colonoscopy stops this war before it begins.
cards.gradeReason: Applying-for-cancer-job is funny but passive — Pete describes surveillance, not a role the player performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro sinister subtle. Subject: Friendly mushroom secretly filling a job application for malignancy. Mood: Quietly menacing.

cards.power: The Pressure Leak. Harry occurs when the venous cushions in the Basement (Anus) swell and prolapse out.
cards.lore: Heavy straining increases intra-abdominal pressure, forcing Harry violently out of his hiding spot.
cards.gradeReason: Cushion-pop under pressure is clear and physical; internal vs external anatomy needs brief orientation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro uncomfortable. Subject: Purple balloons bulging and prolapsing dramatically under straining pressure. Mood: Strained, inevitable.

cards.power: The Knife-Cut. Fred is a small tear in the lining that refuses to heal because the Sphincter-Muscle is spasming.
cards.lore: High sphincter tone causes localized ischemia. Nitro-cream or Botox can force the muscle to relax and let Fred heal.
cards.gradeReason: Knife-cut spasm is viscerally clear; the Botox/Nitro fix is a satisfying punchline needing one beat of context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro painful. Subject: Ferret caught in a spasming sphincter trap, refusing to heal. Mood: Persistent, stinging.

cards.power: The Metabolic Overdrive. Theo controls the match speed. If he goes hyper, the heart races and heat rises.
cards.lore: Cold nodules are more likely to be malignant. Theo's biggest surgery risk is severing the Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve.
cards.gradeReason: Metabolic throttle controller embodied perfectly — go hyper = immediate performance change at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro electric. Subject: Butterfly lodged in throat controlling metabolic dial, sparking at full throttle. Mood: Revved, overheated.

cards.power: The Bone-Breaker. Pat violently steals calcium from the bones and dumps it into the blood and kidneys.
cards.lore: Usually a single Adenoma (Pat's Hideout). Surgery to evict Pat fixes the classic Stones, Bones, Groans, Moans.
cards.gradeReason: Calcium thief + Stones/Bones/Groans/Moans mnemonic = the most table-ready card in the endocrine section.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro heist. Subject: Tiny bandit raiding bones for calcium loot, groaning kidneys in background. Mood: Villainous, greedy.

cards.power: The Adrenaline Surge. Addie creates sudden, massive spikes in blood pressure and heart rate.
cards.lore: Rule of 10%: 10% bilateral, 10% malignant, 10% extra-adrenal. Always Alpha-block before you Beta-block!
cards.gradeReason: Stress Queen embodiment is instant; Alpha-before-Beta rule is surgically urgent and unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro high-voltage. Subject: Bee-queen triggering adrenaline explosion from adrenal gland throne. Mood: Surging, crisis-level.

cards.power: The Crash. Ian releases too much insulin, causing massive hypoglycemia and making the patient faint in the ring.
cards.lore: An islet cell tumor of the pancreas. Ian is incredibly rare but acts as a highly dangerous metabolic assassin.
cards.gradeReason: The Crash is vivid but Whipple's Triad stat keeps one foot in diagnostic-criteria territory.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro dramatic drop. Subject: Bear dumping too much insulin, patient crashing in a sugar snowstorm. Mood: Sudden collapse.

cards.power: The Access Point. Stan achieves the very first goal of any surgical encounter: Exposure.
cards.lore: Stan must collaborate with Yellow Langer's Lines to ensure the final scar heals like a zipper instead of a scream.
cards.gradeReason: Tool inventory card — blade numbers #10/11/15 describe the object, not a character you embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro precise. Subject: Gloved blade hero opening surgical access along Langer's Lines. Mood: Clinical, deliberate.

cards.power: The Duke & Steak. Bill uses high-frequency sparks to cut tissues and literally Fry Bleeding vessels shut.
cards.lore: Bill absolutely requires a Grounding Pad (Return Electrode) or the patient receives a severe accidental Burns.
cards.gradeReason: Frying vessels shut with electric sparks — the most viscerally satisfying procedural card in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro electric grill. Subject: Electric eel cauterizing bleeding vessels with sizzling high-frequency arc. Mood: Crackle, controlled power.

cards.power: The Keyhole View. Leo uses a camera and long chopstick-arms to conduct the entire fight through a tiny hole.
cards.lore: Decreases pain and hospital time. Beware of the Phrenic-Phantom (referred shoulder pain from trapped CO2 gas).
cards.gradeReason: Keyhole minimalist is a clear role; the CO2 Phrenic-Phantom punchline is a gem requiring one step of context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro minimalist. Subject: Chameleon operating through a pinhole with long slender instruments, CO2 ghost hovering. Mood: Precise, contained.

cards.power: The Structural Knot. Sam securely holds the Fascia-Armor together until the body can build its own strength.
cards.lore: Tensile Strength is the absolute law. Sam is the sole reason the Belly-Burst (Dehiscence) doesn't happen.
cards.gradeReason: Clear structural role; absorbable vs permanent stat positions this slightly in technical-criteria zone.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro knot-craft. Subject: Spider weaving tensile sutures across fascia wound, preventing a belly-burst. Mood: Precise, load-bearing.

cards.power: The Life-Sorter. Tim acts as the gatekeeper, deciding who gets the Blade-Brigade first and who has to wait.
cards.lore: In a mass-casualty rampage, you don't save everyone; you ruthlessly optimize to save the most people possible.
cards.gradeReason: Ruthless gatekeeper is a real role; Red/Yellow/Green/Black system needs one orientation beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro authority. Subject: Owl triaging battlefield casualties under four-color flag system. Mood: Grim efficiency, life-or-death calm.

cards.power: The Fluid-Finder. Fiona searches for hidden, pooling blood in Morison's Pouch or around the heart.
cards.lore: If Fiona is positive internally—they bypass the ER and go straight to the OR.
cards.gradeReason: Fluid-finder under ultrasound is purposeful and fast; 4-window anatomy needs quick orientation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro sonar. Subject: Bat with ultrasound probe scanning body cavities for hidden blood pools. Mood: Alert, rapid, decisive.

cards.power: The Lung-Reinflater. Chester aggressively drains air to let the crushed lungs breathe again.
cards.lore: The tube MUST stay above the rib margin to avoid lacerating the Neurovascular Bundle running along the rib.
cards.gradeReason: Lung-reinflater role is clear; the NVB positioning rule is surgical knowledge rather than embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro mechanical. Subject: Armored drain hero wedging into 5th intercostal space, releasing trapped air. Mood: Forceful, relieving.

cards.power: The Consciousness Meter. Gabe instantly tells the trauma surgeon exactly how hard the brain was hit.
cards.lore: GCS of 8, Intubate! If Gabe calculates the score is low, the patient's airway is no longer safe.
cards.gradeReason: A scoring system made into a character — the 3-15 scale describes rather than invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro diagnostic. Subject: Octopus holding consciousness scoreboard with 4/4/5 values. Mood: Clinical, urgent assessment.

cards.power: The Invasive Lump. Max hides in the upper-outer quadrant and slowly spreads his tendrils to the Axillary Node.
cards.lore: Targeted therapy (Tamoxifen) or Wide Local Excision (Lumpectomy) are Max's surgical kryptonite.
cards.gradeReason: Tendrils-to-lymph-nodes is vivid; BI-RADS scoring and staging are clinical overlays needing context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro dark growth. Subject: Dark winged mass invading breast tissue, tendrils reaching toward axillary node. Mood: Insidious, spreading.

cards.power: The First Sentry. Sid is the very first lymph node that Max drains to. If Sid is clear, the army is safe.
cards.lore: Performing a Sentinel Node Biopsy strictly prevents the enormous Lymphedema cost by sparing unnecessary surgery.
cards.gradeReason: Sentry metaphor is elegant but this is a biopsy technique, not a character the player fully inhabits.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro sentinel guard. Subject: Meerkat standing watch at first lymph node checkpoint, biohazard probe scanning. Mood: Vigilant, decisive.

cards.power: The Deep Dive. Mel starts superficially as a dark spot but engages and plunges through the skin layers.
cards.lore: Depth is everything. A low depth is the clinical line in the sand that mandates significantly wider surgical margins.
cards.gradeReason: ABCDE/Breslow criteria are educational mnemonics — Mel describes rather than performs across these stats.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro shadow. Subject: Black panther plunging through skin layers, Breslow depth marker as shadow measurement. Mood: Stealthy, deep.

cards.power: The Fluid-Leech. Ben destroys the skin-barrier, letting the body's plasma evaporate or hemorrhage instantly.
cards.lore: The Parkland Formula is Ben's specific counter-spell. (Massive volume IV resuscitation is the only key to survive.)
cards.gradeReason: Fluid-leech destroying the skin barrier is immediate; Parkland Formula calculation needs one factual context beat.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro scorched. Subject: Fire character dissolving skin barrier, plasma rushing out into evaporation. Mood: Devastating, urgent.

cards.power: The Wound-Split. Dan occurs when Suture-Sam's knot fails and the carefully constructed Belly-Armor tears open.
cards.lore: If the deep Fascia falls and the guts physically fall out, it escalates to Evisceration—live—an absolute surgical nightmare.
cards.gradeReason: Wound-split is immediately kinetic; escalation to evisceration gives this real dramatic urgency.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro bust. Subject: Armadillo armor bursting open post-op, belly-armor sutures snapping one by one. Mood: Catastrophic unraveling.

cards.power: The Shallow Breath. Al closes the tiny Alveolar Balloons because the patient is in too much pain to breathe deeply.
cards.lore: The Incentive Spirometer is the physical counter-spell. You have to force Al to expand and breathe!
cards.gradeReason: Alveolar deflation is mechanistic — the card instructs rather than invites the player to inhabit a role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro deflated. Subject: Flattened lung-balloon creature refusing to expand in a post-op ward. Mood: Stubborn, airless.

cards.power: The Leg-Jam. Doris stops the blood in the calf. If she dislodges and moves to the Lungs, she becomes the deadly PE-Phantom.
cards.lore: Prophylactic Lovenox injections and early walking/ambulation are Doris's sworn enemies.
cards.gradeReason: Leg-Jam becoming a PE-Phantom is pure dramatic escalation — the best clot metaphor in any MedKayfab deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro creeping threat. Subject: Turtle clog forming in calf vein, ghost form rising toward lungs. Mood: Slow then suddenly lethal.

cards.power: The Sleepy Gut. Paul happens when the bowels are handling too roughly during surgery and decide to Go on strike.
cards.lore: Paul is usually temporary. Surprisingly, Chewing Gum and early walking trick the nervous system into waking him up.
cards.gradeReason: Bowels going on strike is endearing and clear; chewing-gum counter-spell is a satisfying punchline needing setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro sleepy. Subject: Worm curled up on strike inside quiet bowel, Zzz floating above absent sounds. Mood: Inert, stubbornly asleep.

cards.power: The Temperature Spike. Fiona tells the surgeon exactly where the hidden infection is located based on post-op timing. Day 1 = Wind (Lungs). Day 3 = Water (UTI). Day 5 = Wound. Day 7 = Walking (DVT).
cards.lore: Day-by-day fever mapping makes every post-op temperature spike a diagnostic performance — immediately actionable.
cards.gradeReason: 5 Ws mnemonic is one of the most usable clinical tools in card format — tables play this immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro ticking fever-clock. Subject: Thermometer character with 5 labeled clock-days revealing a different infection site each. Mood: Systematic urgency.

cards.power: The Total-Body Riot. Sam turns a minor local wound into a global vascular collapse. BP bottoms out; organs fail.
cards.lore: Massive vasodilation. Sepsis-Sam desperately needs 30ml/kg of Crystalloid Juice and immediate broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
cards.gradeReason: Total-body riot / global vascular collapse — the most terrifying single character in the post-op section.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro systemic chaos. Subject: Dragon igniting global vascular riot, organ failures cascading in a ring collapse. Mood: Catastrophic, racing.

cards.power: The Tank-Drain. Hank is the silent killer. Blood is rapidly leaving the system, and the patient is getting dangerously sleepy.
cards.lore: Class I to IV hemorrhagic shock. By Class III, crystalloids aren't enough—you need Liquid Gold (Blood transfusions).
cards.gradeReason: Tank draining into dangerous sleepiness — visceral, quiet, and terrifying. Liquid Gold counter is unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro draining. Subject: Red spider silently draining blood tank, patient slumping through hemorrhagic stages. Mood: Silent, deadly.

cards.power: The Metabolic Inferno. A rare, lethal reaction to anesthetic gas that turns the patient's body into an uncontrollable oven.
cards.lore: Defect in the Ryanodine receptor. The specialized drug Dantrolene— is the absolute only weapon that can stop Annie.
cards.gradeReason: Uncontrollable metabolic oven with one singular antidote — the most dramatically defined emergency in the entire deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro furnace horror. Subject: Iguana inside a glass oven body, temperature spiking uncontrolled, Dantrolene as sole lifeline. Mood: Infernal, rare.

cards.power: The Legal Shield. Ensures the patient actively knows exactly what Anatomical trespassing is about to legally occur.
cards.lore: Emergency-implied consent only exists when the patient is completely unconscious, dying, and unable to speak for themselves.
cards.gradeReason: Anatomical trespassing framing is clever; the implied-consent exception needs legal context to fully embody.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro bureaucratic. Subject: Stork clerk presenting surgical consent form as legal shield before the cut. Mood: Formal, protective.

cards.power: The Germ-Wall. The Siren rigidly ensures no Microbe-Monsters hitch a ride into the sterile Surgical Scrimmage.
cards.lore: Blue is Sterile. In the operating theatre, anything that isn't draped in sterile blue is treated as a lethal threat.
cards.gradeReason: Blue-is-sterile is the most visually immediate rule in perioperative medicine — clear but needs the theatre orientation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro pristine. Subject: Swan-armored sterility guardian in blue drapes blocking all microbe invaders at the OR door. Mood: Immaculate, rigid.

cards.power: The Final Verdict. They dictate via microscope if the Cancer-Monster is fully gone, or if the surgeon needs to cut wider.
cards.lore: Frozen sections give an intraoperative answer in minutes; permanent Formalin sections take days to process.
cards.gradeReason: A lab-process card — the microscope work describes procedure rather than inviting table-side embodiment.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro forensic. Subject: Bloodhound biopsy team examining tissue slides under microscope for cancer verdict. Mood: Deliberate, definitive.

cards.power: The Wake-Up Call. The Ranger guards and monitors the patient as their brain slowly reboots post-battle.
cards.lore: Airway, Pain, and Pulse are the three deadly enemies that the Ranger must fight in the Post-Anesthesia Care Unit.
cards.gradeReason: PACU monitoring is a process checklist — Aldrete scoring describes rather than invites performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro watchful. Subject: Saint Bernard guarding waking patient in PACU, tracking airway, pain, and pulse dials. Mood: Gentle vigil.

cards.power: The Master-Trespasser. He oversees the Scrimmage, ensuring no one blindly cuts without understanding the Lore.
cards.lore: Is the patient stable? Is the anatomy clear? Why are you still holding the Bovie when you should be tying? Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: The meta-attending who questions every move — the most playable authority card in any MedKayfab deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro boss-mode. Subject: FrizzleBob-rabbit in attending scrubs holding X-ray, questioning the whole surgical scrimmage. Mood: Commanding, fluffy.

cards.power: Scenario: A 45yo female presents with sharp RUQ pain after eating a pizza. You press under her Ribs, and she stops breathing.
cards.lore: Identify the Stone-Collector (Chole-Cathy) causing this acute cholecystitis. Is this a conservative scan day or an urgent OR day?
cards.gradeReason: Murphy's Sign as a live clinical scenario — players perform the physical exam and make the decision immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro clinical. Subject: Wolf clutching RUQ, Murphy's Sign triggered mid-exam, scan vs OR decision fork in foreground. Mood: Acute, urgent choice.

cards.power: Scenario: A patient 5 days after a complex colon resection reports a sudden Pop and serosanguinous fluid leaking from the wound.
cards.lore: Identify the Burst (Dehiscence-Dan). Assess the immediate mechanical risk of the Bowel-Spill (Evisceration).
cards.gradeReason: A post-op emergency players diagnose and triage live — the evisceration escalation makes it unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro emergency. Subject: Bear patient clutching burst surgical wound, intestines threatening to spill at day 5. Mood: Panic, post-op catastrophe.

cards.power: Scenario: An elderly patient presents with a massive, hard belly. X-Ray shows a giant Coffee Bean filling up the screen.
cards.lore: Name the Strangler (Volvulus-Val) and urgently describe the exact mechanism of this life-threatening vascular choke-point.
cards.gradeReason: Coffee-Bean X-ray is one of surgery's most iconic image findings — recognizing it at the table is pure performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Kayfabizarro X-ray drama. Subject: Elderly patient with giant coffee-bean volvulus on X-ray, Volvulus Val circling the mesentery. Mood: Iconic, alarming.

verdict: The Surgical Scrimmage is the strongest single-specialty MedKayfab deck yet — 56 cards covering surgical emergencies, hernia, vascular, upper GI, colorectal, endocrine, oncology, procedural tools, trauma, post-op complications, and perioperative medicine with no gaps. The character naming convention (Archie Appendicitis, Strangulated-Stan, Anesthesia-Annie) is consistently brilliant, and the three Synthesis Quest cards turn the deck into a simulation engine unique among ADD releases. The procedural/instrumental block (Scalpel-Stan, GCS-Gabe, Pathology-Pack, Recovery-Ranger) drops to G3 because they describe processes rather than characters to inhabit. The cover — FrizzleBob in a wrestling ring made of a jawbone — is the best MedKayfab cover produced to date. Table-ready Y.
blurb: For med students who'd rather perform an acute abdomen than memorize one — 56 surgery characters from Archie Appendicitis to Anesthesia-Annie, with three live clinical scenarios that turn flashcards into surgical emergencies.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob-rabbit in surgical scrubs inside a wrestling ring formed by a giant jawbone/teeth motif — spectacular, unexpected, high-craft illustration
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'A chance to cut is a chance to cure. Stay fluffy!' is a perfect surgical tagline with full character voice
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Surgical Scrimmage theme is fully realized in every visual element — zero mismatch
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Among the highest originality in the MedKayfab series; the jaw-ring concept is genuinely surprising
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Strong viral potential especially for surgery/med student communities; FrizzleBob context amplifies it further
coverQA.coverNote: Best MedKayfab cover so far. The wrestling-ring-as-jawbone concept is a fresh compositional idea not appearing in any prior deck. The tagline 'A chance to cut is a chance to cure' is surgical mnemonics reframed perfectly.
